hypotheses.justification: Choose a shortest finite chain from u to v whose consecutive forward matrix entries are nonzero. Such a chain exists: Reachable supplies a walk, and getVert_zero, getVert_length, adj_getVert_succ, and diagramGraph_adj give the required endpoints and nonzero entries without h. Minimality implies injectivity, since any repeated vertex permits deleting the intervening segment. It also implies the final vanishing condition: a nonzero entry from position i to position j with i + 1 < j permits shortcutting that segment, contradicting minimality. Minimize over matrix chains, not diagram walks, so no symmetric vanishing assumption is needed. Extend the chosen finite chain to ℕ using u. If u = v, the length-zero chain works; empty B cannot supply u. Thus neither finiteness nor the other finite-type conditions are required.
